Multi-Sensor Fusion for Long-Tailed 3D Object Detection

BEVFusion + DINO late fusion vs. CenterPoint + DINO, with class-balanced fine-tuning — results on nuScenes trainval (part-1 val)

  • Evaluation set: 914 samples / 23 scenes (nuScenes trainval part-1 val, fixed across all experiments)
  • 3D backbones (CenterPoint, BEVFusion): frozen, pretrained, inference only
  • Only the 2D camera detector (DINO) is fine-tuned across experiments

1.Pipeline Overview

A frozen 3D detector (LiDAR only) is combined with a fine-tuned 2D camera detector (DINO) via late fusion. The two detectors run as independent strands over the same sample and are only combined at the fusion step. Two 3D backbones are compared as drop-in replacements: CenterPoint and BEVFusion.

Late fusion
project · match · fuse
↓
Output
fused boxes, evaluated
Fusion procedure: each 3D box is projected onto the 6 camera images (lidar2cam + cam2img). Per camera and class, an IoU cost matrix between projected 3D boxes and DINO's 2D boxes is solved via the Hungarian algorithm. Matches above IoU 0.5 are combined with a Bayesian score fusion using per-class calibration constants adapted from Ma et al. (lt3d-lf). Visible-but-unmatched 3D boxes are down-weighted by 0.5.

nuScenes trainval, downloaded incrementally. The evaluation set is held fixed across every experiment below.

Validation set (fixed)

914 samples, 23 scenes — trainval part 1 only. A subset of the official 150-scene val split: results are internally consistent across experiments, but not directly comparable to published SOTA numbers.

3.3D Detector Baselines (No DINO Fusion)

LiDAR-only inference from each frozen 3D backbone, before any camera fusion.

4.CenterPoint + DINO

Baseline replication of the Peri et al. / Ma et al. late-fusion approach with DINO fine-tuned on the imbalanced class distribution (Run A).

5.BEVFusion + DINO — Main Experiment Grid

BEVFusion as the 3D backbone, with DINO fine-tuned under different class-balancing strategies.

Curated Selective Ingestion

Pools additional real trainval parts and curates the image set — keeps every tail-containing image, drops most car/pedestrian-only images. Produced the best standalone 2D detector (2D val mAP 0.251) but a worse fused result: a barrier regression (0.590 → 0.423) that a calibration sweep confirmed was not correctable via fusion tuning.

Curated + Oversampling complete

Direct, same-data comparison against oversampled run: identical part-1 scenes and ClassBalancedDataset settings, the only difference is curating away most car/pedestrian-only images first. Result below.

Curating before oversampling reduces total training volume (8,815 vs 14,772 images), which cost the rarest classes (construction_vehicle −0.029, trailer −0.022) more than the improved relative balance gained back. barrier is the exception, reaching its best result across all runs (0.619) — since this run uses part-1 data only, this points to the added real data in the "Curated" run (not class balance) as the likely cause of barrier's regression there.

8.Key Findings

1. Main claim confirmed

BEVFusion + DINO outperforms CenterPoint + DINO at every matched DINO fine-tuning variant.

2. Diminishing returns for camera-aware backbones

DINO fusion adds more to CenterPoint (+0.05–0.07 overall mAP) than to BEVFusion (+0.02) — BEVFusion already uses camera features internally.

3. Oversampling outperforms data curation

ClassBalancedDataset raises the relative frequency of scarce classes independently per class. Curation only grows absolute counts, which can worsen relative imbalance for some classes (construction_vehicle, motorcycle) even as it helps others.

4. A fusion ceiling for the rarest classes

For trailer and construction_vehicle, a better 2D detector did not move the fused AP. Late fusion can only reweight 3D boxes the frozen backbone already produced.

Training-seed variance (Run C, measured Aug 11)

Retrained Run C twice more with fixed seeds (seed=1, seed=2) to establish the noise floor. Overall mAP spread: 0.634–0.636 (±0.002). Tail mAP spread: 0.560–0.563 (±0.003). This confirms every major finding in this project (barrier's 0.152 collapse, oversampled vs curated Δ0.016–0.022) is well above the noise floor and reflects real effects, not seed-driven randomness.

Fusion hyperparameter sweep (Aug 12)

Swept IOU_THRESH (0.3–0.7), SCORE_3D_THR (0.02–0.15), and W_UNMATCHED (0.3–1.0) on the oversampled run's cached predictions. Best found: IOU_THRESH=0.3 → overall 0.640, a +0.004 gain — at the edge of the measured noise floor. Confirms the original fusion parameters were already near-optimal.

Barrier diagnostic chain (Aug 10–12)

A 5-step investigation into why barrier collapses under multi-part+oversampled training (0.590 → 0.438): (1) label geometry — no difference, (2) 2D AP — unchanged, (3) fusion calibration sweep — ceiling ~0.453, (4) barrier excluded from oversampling — no recovery, (5) barrier volume partially reduced — worsened. Root cause: training on combined multi-part data shifts barrier's confidence distribution (more hallucinated FPs at score>0.3, precision 0.671→0.518), which is not isolable to any single, fixable mechanism.
